Hi Hoto,

There is no single rule to find where you want to trade. We trade supply and demand, lot of people trade ranges, support and resistance, trend line, Fibonaccis and what not. All these places are good enough to see price action. A DBD or a RBD, they both are a good places to look for PA, and if PA is happening at any place where it makes sense to happen, our duty is to take that trade.

We dont need to make a million analysis before taking every trade....keep your Reward:Risk high enough, trade with some kind of logical setup which gives you winning trades, and you are on your way.

Settle down on a setup which you like to trade, observe it like hell, in every time frame, every situation, every place it forms, trade it and see when it works, when it does not work. Think why it worked and why it did not work. You can ask 1000 questions, no body here at RTM will mind, we all are here to help each other, that is the motive or RTM, but in the end, it will come down to you and your trading style. Understand your trading style like the back of your hand and you will be all good. You dont need a 100 ways to trade, find 1 that suits your style.

Feel free to ask as many questions as you want, I will try my best to answer them. If I can not, I am sure somebody else will definitely.

Good luck man.

Hey hoto,

As Sunny says, keep the questions coming. To wait for engulfs on the higher TF only will take quite a long time and we wouldn't get many trades. We can do this successfully on lower TF as well. Also, I would absolutely look at a combination of time frames when price is in a daily or H4 zone, even 5min charts. The important thing to remember here is we are looking for reactions, for signs price wants to move away from an important level. These important levels can be, as sunny says anything, they can be flip zones, SD zones, SR levels. Once price reaches these levels in any time-frame we can look for engulfings on a smaller time frame to trade them.

There are ample trades on daily and H4 and the wait is not actually that long.

EURJPY recently engulfed north towards supply level.

The engulf created a nice demand level. When price returned to the level it moved north nicely. Price is now directly in supply zone.

I think this is why I get confused when I read posts from different people. I see that the high that was engulfed is the origination of the move that put the low in. So I understand why you picked that level as the significant one that was engulfed, but why did you go to lower time frames and pick the level that you did to go long? Why not go long at the bottom of the flag pole on the daily? That would put you at the origination of the move up that made the engulf. The 4hr level seems to be in the middle of the move, not the origination. All of the other posts I have been looking at involve two basic things. An engulf of an important level, and an entry at the origination of that move that did the engulfing.

Hello Hotochin,

I have marked the origin of the engulf I am speaking of. It is certainly a nice level and when price comes back it will definitely be a level to consider carefully. I think you are speaking of this origin being a reaction to a demand level left which it does appear it was. But I am speaking of this most current engulf north. I understand an engulf to be an important overcoming of a significant portion of price action such that the probability that price will continue in that direction is higher. In this case price engulfed north ( I have the point of the engulf marked by the white line). Institutional money causes such an engulf and when it does it leaves it's signature which is the creation of more levels. In this case when price engulfed north pockets of demand were created. The daily chart doesn't show them that well but the H4 chart is more revealing.

Before price reached the supply marked overhead a return to one of the demand levels marked had an increased probability of causing price to rise to the supply level which it has and is currently in. Now that price is in a significant supply zone dynamics could change with sellers stepping in and driving price back down again to one of the lower demand zones. I don't know what will happen but when big money steps in they will again leave their signatures by engulfing south and creating new supply levels. I am not opposed to trading levels midstream if the dynamics are in favor.

Since I am trading H4 and up I will open positions at clearly defined "midzone" levels. have found that price responds quite nicely to midzone levels and often may not revisit the origin for some time. By the time it does revisit the origin the dynamics may have changed and price may violate the origin. If you are trading M1 and M5 it's probably better to go with extremes.
